findings.title: Selection normalization precedes checksum verification and accepts a digest that does not bind the received dictionary
findings.observed: For all five selection set dimensions, appending a duplicate or permuting two entries changes the canonical received package dictionary hash without changing the declared digest. decode_package accepts all thirty dict/str/bytes variants, reconstructs the normalized original selection and returns the stale digest. Conversely, supplying the actual changed dictionary digest is rejected as DIGEST_MISMATCH in the ten standalone measured probes.
findings.cause: decode_package constructs ExchangeSelectionScope before ExchangePackage recomputes the checksum. ExchangeSelectionScope.to_dict sorts and deduplicates set dimensions; _canonical_content hashes package.to_dict rather than the received dictionary.
findings.impact: The public v5 codec's checksum does not cover the entire received package dictionary excluding only digest_sha256 as required by R03. This is transport integrity/canonicality failure, not sender authentication or an established admission/authorization bypass.
findings.attribution: Independently reproduced in #149 v4 and #151 v5 with actual imports bound to separate archived trees. The mechanism is inherited; its persistence violates the newly frozen v5 R03 contract. No production regression claim is made for #151 relative to #149.
acceptance_criteria: Verify SHA-256 over the actual bounded received dictionary excluding only digest_sha256 before converting selection into a normalizing domain type, or reject noncanonical set arrays before accepting the envelope without silently repairing them.
Refuse every independently saved stale-digest duplicate/permutation vector across dict/str/bytes carriers, while valid canonical-selection packages continue to roundtrip.
Exercise the unchanged independent required-refusal probes on source and both newly built installed distributions; preserve exact node/phase/process evidence.
Retain the distinction between canonical-data integrity, unauthenticated Provider claims and current admission authority; leave both Transfer fences intact.

informational_observations.topic: Core primitive validation remains a downstream semantic boundary
informational_observations.observation: Eight malformed Core repository/OID primitive variants are accepted by decode_package both at #149 and #151, but all eight are refused by the actual CorePreflight/typed OID constructor boundary. The pure envelope API is expressly untrusted and no public admission bypass is inferred. This observation is not counted as a new Medium finding.
